title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit
plain: The computer is watching the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor and has spotted a fault in its circuit. It reports how much vacuum is stored for systems such as the brake booster or emissions actuators.
symptoms: Brake pedal may feel harder than normal
Some vacuum-operated controls may not work

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor
Broken or chafed wire in the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor circuit
Missing reference voltage or ground from the computer

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor.

title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The computer is watching the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. It reports how much vacuum is stored for systems such as the brake booster or emissions actuators.
symptoms: Brake pedal may feel harder than normal
Some vacuum-operated controls may not work

causes.name: Failing or sticking vacuum reservoir pressure sensor
Vacuum leak or weak vacuum pump
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Find out whether the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor itself or the system it works with is at fault, then repair or replace as needed.

title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
plain: The computer is watching the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor and is reading a voltage that is lower than it should be, which often means a short to ground or a failed part. It reports how much vacuum is stored for systems such as the brake booster or emissions actuators.
symptoms: Brake pedal may feel harder than normal
Some vacuum-operated controls may not work

causes.name: Signal wire in the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor shorted to ground or open

checks: Inspect the wiring in the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Unplug the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor and see if the reading changes
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor.

title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit High
plain: The computer is watching the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor and is reading a voltage that is higher than it should be, which often means a broken ground or a short to power. It reports how much vacuum is stored for systems such as the brake booster or emissions actuators.
symptoms: Brake pedal may feel harder than normal
Some vacuum-operated controls may not work

causes.name: Signal wire shorted to voltage or a broken ground wire

checks: Inspect the wiring and ground connection for the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor
Check for wires melted or rubbed together in the harness
Measure the circuit with a meter before replacing parts
fix: Repair the open ground or shorted wire; if the wiring is fine, replace the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor.

title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
plain: The computer is watching the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor and is seeing a signal that cuts in and out. It reports how much vacuum is stored for systems such as the brake booster or emissions actuators.
symptoms: Brake pedal may feel harder than normal
Some vacuum-operated controls may not work

causes.name: Loose connector or chafed wire that loses contact over bumps
Vacuum reservoir pressure sensor failing on and off

checks: Wiggle the wiring for the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor with the engine running while watching live data
Check connector pins for corrosion or spread terminals
Note when it happens (hot, cold, bumps) to narrow it down
fix: Repair the loose or corroded connection; replace the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor if the wiring is solid.

title: Engine Oil Level Too High
plain: The oil level sensor says there is too much oil in the engine. Overfilling can cause foamy oil and leaks.
symptoms: Oil level warning or check engine light on

causes.name: Engine overfilled at the last oil change
Fuel or coolant getting into the oil

checks: Check the oil level on level ground
Smell the oil for fuel and look for a milky color
Drain to the correct level if overfilled
fix: Drain the extra oil; if the level keeps rising, find where the fuel or coolant is coming from.

title: Engine Oil Deteriorated
plain: The car has worked out that the engine oil is worn out and needs changing.
symptoms: Check engine light or oil service warning on
Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Lots of short trips, towing or idling wearing out the oil faster
Oil life monitor not reset after the last change

checks: Check when the oil was last changed
Change the oil and reset the oil life monitor
fix: Change the oil and filter, then reset the oil life reminder.

title: Torque Management Request Input Signal "A"
plain: The computer is watching the torque management request signal and has spotted a fault in its circuit. Another module (often the transmission computer) uses this signal to ask the engine to cut power briefly, such as during shifts.

causes.name: Wiring or connector fault between the engine and transmission computers
Module software that needs an update

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the torque management request signal, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or network fault, or update the module software as the maker directs.
